item.description: Greek authorities released the second group of defendants in the Crete OPEKEPE illegal subsidy case after they testified before the examining magistrate. The three individuals who appeared today, including the accountant’s wife, were freed on the condition that they remain in Greece. item.title: Syriza MEP Nikos Pappas Suspended After Alleged Assault on Journalist in Strasbourg
item.description: Greek MEP Nikos Pappas has been suspended from Syriza and faces potential expulsion after allegedly assaulting journalist Nikos Giannopoulos in a Strasbourg bar on December 16, 2025. The reporter claims Pappas tripped him, challenged him to fight outside, and struck him twice on the head from behind, leading to a police complaint and investigation not covered by MEP immunity. item.title: Paphos Art Exhibition Shut Down Amid Blasphemy Row and Death Threats
item.description: A controversial art exhibition by Cypriot painter Giorgos Gavriil titled "Antisystemic Art" was shut down in Paphos less than 24 hours after opening due to public outrage and death threats over works depicting Christ and the Virgin Mary in provocative political contexts. The Blue Iris Gallery cited societal opposition and safety concerns, sparking debate on artistic freedom versus religious sensitivity in Cyprus. item.title: Hormuz Island Seas Turn Blood-Red After Rains
item.description: Heavy rains in mid-December 2025 caused iron-rich red soil to wash into the sea around Iran's Hormuz Island, turning coastal waters a vivid blood-red hue and evoking Biblical references to the Nile turning to blood in the Plague of Egypt. This stunning natural geological phenomenon, often called "blood rain," has gone viral, attracting tourists to the UNESCO geopark's colorful landscapes. item.title: Netanyahu Announces Israel's Largest-Ever Gas Deal with Egypt Worth NIS 112 Billion
item.description: Israel has approved its largest-ever natural gas export deal with Egypt, worth NIS 112 billion ($35 billion), Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced on December 17, 2025. The agreement from the Leviathan reservoir will bring NIS 58 billion directly to state coffers, boost regional energy ties, and potentially pave the way for diplomatic progress.
